changed.title: The solution-count matrix for two families of local Boolean tests has rank two to the number of shared variables
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n l r : ℕ)
  (L : Fin l → Finset (Fin n)) (R : Fin r → Finset (Fin n)),
  (∀ v : Fin n, (∃ i, v ∈ L i) ∨ ∃ j, v ∈ R j) →
  let S := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter
    (fun v => (∃ i, v ∈ L i) ∧ ∃ j, v ∈ R j)
  let Left := (i : Fin l) → ((↥(L i) → Bool) → Bool)
  let Right := (j : Fin r) → ((↥(R j) → Bool) → Bool)
  let count := fun (p : Left) (q : Right) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Bool)).filter (fun x =>
      (∀ i, p i (fun v => x v.val) = true) ∧
      (∀ j, q j (fun v => x v.val) = true))).card
  ∀ d : ℕ,
    (∃ (A : Left → Fin d → K) (B : Right → Fin d → K),
      ∀ p q, (count p q : K) = ∑ j : Fin d, A p j * B q j) ↔
    2 ^ S.card ≤ d
changed.unlocks: determines the rank of a local table solution-count matrix over every field from its shared variable count
changed.context: Group solutions by their shared assignment. For each assignment, count extensions on each side using only sites on that side, then multiply. Pad these coordinates by zeros. Conversely, for each shared string pin every private bit to zero and let each local table accept exactly the restriction of this assignment. Matching pins have one solution and mismatched pins have none. The resulting identity matrix factors through the same d coordinates, forcing 2^s ≤ d over every field. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a matrix rank.

changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Keep columns 0,1,5 and rows 0,1,2. Delete columns 2,3,4 and row 3 one at a time. Each live duplicate costs at least one first-reader gate by fixing its wire to zero. Reorder the three rows as 0,2,1 and the three columns as 1,0,5, then pad both banks with a zero site. The result is four-by-four mask 293. A size-nine witness gives size five, contradicting checked L-meta-5506.

changed.title: It is false that: Find a six-gate four-row selector with ordered pair and triple witnesses and free column features
changed.statement:
¬ (∃ (G : Fin 4 → Fin 6 → Bool) (code : Fin 6 → Fin 4 → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  (∀ u v : Fin 4, u ≠ v → ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) ∧
  (∀ u v w : Fin 4, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 6 ∧
  ∀ (u : Fin 4) (c : Fin 6),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin 4 => decide (i = u)) ++ List.ofFn (code c)) = G u c)
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Take the alleged four-row, six-column table, its four free column features and its circuit. Specialize the checked row-selector lower bound to n=4, m=6, p=4. The ordered-pair and ordered-triple hypotheses and every one-hot evaluation are supplied by the witness. The bound gives seven gates, contradicting its size of at most six. Four row-feature ANDs joined by three ORs give the seven-gate control using the six unordered row pairs as columns.

changed.title: Which prescribed pairwise witnesses extend to exact three-owner ternary CNFs for physical cyclic window feasibility
changed.statement:
∀ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (owner : Fin n → Fin 3),
  let Word := Fin n → Bool
  let Pattern := Fin (w+1) → Bool
  let pos := fun (r : Fin n) (d : Fin (w+1)) =>
    (⟨(r.val + d.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let window := fun (x : Word) (r : Fin n) (d : Fin (w+1)) => x (pos r d)
  (∀ (party : Fin 3) (z : Fin n), ∃ r : Fin n, owner r = party ∧
    ∃ d : Fin (w+1), pos r d = z) →
  ∀ (k : Fin 3 → ℕ) (ternary : Bool),
    let next := fun e : Fin 3 => e + 1
    let Msg := (e : Fin 3) → Fin (k e) → Bool
    let Table := Fin n → Pattern → Bool
    let pins := fun (word : Word) (row : Fin n) (pat : Pattern) => decide (pat = window word row)
    let V := fun (p : Fin 3) (q : ℕ) =>
      Sum ({r : Fin n // owner r = p} × Pattern)
        (Sum ((e : {t : Fin 3 // t = p ∨ next t = p}) × Fin (k e.val)) (Fin q))
    ∀ code : Word → Msg,
      (∃ (priv : Fin 3 → ℕ) (F : (p : Fin 3) → Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (V p (priv p)))),
        let accepts := fun (tab : Table) (y : Msg) => ∀ p : Fin 3, ∃ a : Fin (priv p) → Bool,
          PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies
            (Sum.elim (fun h : {i : Fin n // owner i = p} × Pattern => tab h.1.val h.2)
              (Sum.elim (fun bit : (e : {t : Fin 3 // t = p ∨ next t = p}) × Fin (k e.val) =>
                y bit.1.val bit.2) a)) (↑(F p) : Set _)
        (ternary = true → ∀ p, ∀ C ∈ F p, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
        (∀ T : Table, (∃ x : Word, ∀ i, T i (window x i) = true) ↔ ∃ transcript, accepts T transcript) ∧
        ∀ x : Word, accepts (pins x) (code x)) ↔
      ∀ chosen : Fin 3 → Word,
        (∀ e : Fin 3, code (chosen e) e = code (chosen (next e)) e) →
        ∀ party : Fin 3, chosen party = chosen 0
changed.unlocks: characterizes the channel selections that extend to a local ternary encoding
changed.context: For each word give every row its unique window of that word and use the prescribed accepting transcript. If the three owners choose words agreeing on the transcript of each shared channel, splice their rows and private witnesses. Every owner sees every physical position, so feasibility forces all three words equal. Conversely each owner guesses a word, checks its own rows and its two channel values against the code. Three passing guesses coincide by hypothesis. Encode these finite local tests by CNFs with private ternary gates.

changed.title: Majority of 8 bits (at least 4 on): at most 25 AND, OR, NOT gates, none dead, a NOT on a gate
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 8 C ∧ C.size ≤ 25 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 8 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = decide (4 ≤ (List.ofFn x).count true)) ∧ (∀ j < C.size, C.output = 8 + j ∨ ∃ i < C.size, j < i ∧ 8 + j ∈ (C.gates.getD i ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).inputs) ∧ (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not → 8 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0 → (C.gates.getD (g.inputs.headD 0 - 8) ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).op ≠ PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) ∧ (∃ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧ 8 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0)
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can be at work at the best known size for this function
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 7 the inputs, gate j writes wire 8+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 25 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted, so a yes is a circuit with a NOT at work that ties it. A circuit where the NOT and the gate reading it can be deleted and the rest is still right satisfies this row and shows nothing; say whether yours survives that deletion. So does a NOT-free circuit three gates smaller with one gate rewritten through NOTs; say if yours is one.
changed.sketch: A circuit three gates below our NOT-free bar also answers this; a calibration of our constructions, no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 7 the inputs, gate j writes wire 8+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 25 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted. A NOT-free circuit of 22 gates with its last gate rewritten through NOTs meets every clause, and so does a circuit whose NOT can be deleted; say which kind yours is.

changed.title: Products of disjoint block monomials lose degree wherever a polynomial-query list predicts every coordinate
changed.statement:
∀ (m r c d L t : Nat), c < r → 0 < L → 0 < t →
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let par := fun (z : Nat) => z % 2 == 1
  let deg := fun (u : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ u) ∧
      ∀ word, f word = par ((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, word j = true)).card)
  let productOn := fun (I : Finset (Fin m)) (x : W) =>
    decide (∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j : Fin r, x (i,j) = true)
  let run := fun (steps : Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (x : W) =>
    (List.range steps).foldl (fun past pos => past + ((ask pos past x).toNat <<< pos)) 0
  ∀ (budget : Fin d → Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool)
    (leaf : Nat → Fin L → Fin m → W → Bool),
    (∑ j : Fin d, budget j) < (r-c)*t →
    (∀ (u : Fin d) (path : Nat), deg (budget u) (ask u.val path)) →
    (∀ path a i, deg c (leaf path a i)) →
    let hit := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun sample =>
      ∃ a, ∀ i, leaf (run d ask sample) a i sample = decide (∀ v : Fin r, sample (i,v) = true))
    ∀ I : Finset (Fin m), I.card = L*t →
      ∃ q : W → Bool, deg (r*I.card-1) q ∧ ∀ x ∈ hit, q x = productOn I x
changed.unlocks: Lowers the degree of a selected block product on the entire list success set.
changed.context: Partition the selected blocks into L groups of t. On each leaf form a product with one factor per candidate, the true group product plus that candidate’s product of its t predictions. A hit makes this expression zero. Its leading term is the full true monomial. Every other term loses at least (r-c)t degrees. Multiply only the lower terms by their leaf indicators, of degree at most D, and add over leaves. Exactly one leaf indicator is one, so the sum replaces the leading term on every hit.

changed.title: Promise-Ball-SAT uses b branches when every initially false clause has at most b variables and width is at most b+1 (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n b r : Nat), 0 < b →
  let V := Fin n
  let Point := V → Bool
  let Clause := Finset (V × Bool)
  let sat := fun (formula : Finset Clause) (x : Point) =>
    ∀ c ∈ formula, ∃ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 = lit.2
  ∀ (clauses : List Clause) (center : Point),
    let F := clauses.toFinset
    let bad := fun (x : Point) (c : Clause) => ∀ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 ≠ lit.2
    let vars := fun (c : Clause) => c.image Prod.fst
    let state := fun (flipped : Finset V) (v : V) =>
      if v ∈ flipped then !(center v) else center v
    let run := fun (choices : Fin r → Fin b) =>
      (List.finRange r).foldl (fun used step =>
        let c := (clauses.find? (fun d => decide (bad (state used) d))).getD ∅
        let options := ((vars c) \ used).sort (· ≤ ·)
        let picked := options[ (choices step).val ]?
        used ∪ picked.toList.toFinset) (∅ : Finset V)
    (∀ c ∈ F, (vars c).card ≤ b+1) →
    (∀ c ∈ F, bad center c → (vars c).card ≤ b) →
    (∃ y : Point, sat F y ∧ ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun i => y i ≠ center i)).card ≤ r) ↔
      ∃ choices : Fin r → Fin b, sat F (state (run choices))
changed.unlocks: Prices the local search after restriction on a small disjoint packing of false clauses.
changed.context: Maintain agreement of flipped bits with a chosen nearby model. A false clause has an unflipped variable on which the current word differs from that model. If it was false initially it has at most b variables. If it was true initially, at least one of its at most b+1 variables is already flipped. Hence a valid branch selects the useful variable and reduces distance by one. Once satisfied, all remaining steps are idle. Conversely the procedure flips at most r bits.

If it was false initially it has at most b variables. If it was true initially, at least one of its at most b+1 variables is already flipped. Hence a valid branch selects the useful variable and reduces distance by one. Once satisfied, all remaining steps are idle. Conversely the procedure flips at most r bits.

changed.title: A sharp binomial bound for sets where all products of k complete blocks agree with lower-degree polynomials
changed.statement:
∀ (m r k : Nat), 0 < r → 0 < k →
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let par := fun (z : Nat) => z % 2 == 1
  let deg := fun (u : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ u) ∧
      ∀ word, f word = par ((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, word j = true)).card)
  let productOn := fun (I : Finset (Fin m)) (x : W) =>
    decide (∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j : Fin r, x (i,j) = true)
  let budget := (Finset.range (m+1)).sum (fun j =>
    if j < k then Nat.choose m j * (2^r-1)^(m-j) else 0)
  let lowers := fun (S : Finset W) => ∀ I : Finset (Fin m), I.card = k →
    ∃ q : W → Bool, deg (r*k-1) q ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, q x = productOn I x
  (∀ S : Finset W, lowers S → S.card ≤ budget) ∧
  let extremal := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun sample =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter (fun i => ∀ j : Fin r, sample (i,j) = true)).card < k)
  lowers extremal ∧ extremal.card = budget
changed.unlocks: Converts lower-degree identities for many whole blocks into a binomial count of successful inputs.
changed.context: In a squarefree monomial containing k complete blocks, extract their product, substitute its lower-degree representative on S, and multiply by the leftover variables. Every term has strictly smaller degree. Induct until the monomials contain at most k-1 complete blocks. They span every function on S, including point indicators. Count these monomials by choosing the complete blocks and a proper subset in each other block. On the stated extremal set the selected products all vanish.
changed.sketch: In a squarefree monomial containing k complete blocks, extract their product, substitute its lower-degree representative on S, and multiply by the leftover variables. Every term has strictly smaller degree. Induct until the monomials contain at most k-1 complete blocks. They span every function on S, including point indicators. Count these monomials by choosing the complete blocks and a proper subset in each other block. On the stated extremal set the selected products all vanish.
